rationale: Owner decision 2026-09-02 (relayed by the lendzy lane with the worked method): the five register-less finance sites named in RFC_060 §1b build their evidence registers — loancalculator.co.uk is one. Today the site has ZERO evidence_base rows [MEASURED 2026-09-02], so ScanUnregisteredNumbers never arms (HasScannableRegister is the opt-in) and the daily citation refresher passes over an empty set — a green that means nothing. RFC_060 §4: populating these registers 'belongs to the site lanes, needs no RFC, and would deliver most of the benefit of (ii) without any code at all. If only one thing happens as a result of this RFC, it should be that.' Method followed = lendzy's RUNBOOK §8 / migration 695, step for step: (1) all 28 served pages crawled and 232 regulatory-shaped sentences extracted FROM THE ARTEFACT; (2) every governing provision fetched and READ — unlike lendzy this site's assertions are dominated by Consumer Credit Act 1974 rights (settlement figures, voluntary termination, 14-day withdrawal, default notices, dealer-as-agent), so the register cites legislation.gov.uk for statutes alongside handbook.fca.org.uk for CONC/DISP rules, and the daily refresher re-fetches ANY citation URL so both hosts get the same daily re-check; (3) every URL confirmed by <title>, never status (the handbook 200s-every-path LANDMINE, applied to both hosts); (4) all 12 quotes verified through the PRODUCTION matcher (cmd/fcaquotecheck → datahelpers.VisibleTextFromHTML/QuoteFoundInText), 12/12 true with the deliberately-absent control false in the same runs. The exercise caught the site twice, exactly as it did on lendzy: the settlement page says the written figure arrives 'usually within ten working days' (it is TWELVE — SI 1983/1564 reg 4, quoted verbatim), and the overpayment page attributes a '10% of outstanding balance per 12 months' ERC-free allowance to the CCA (no such rule exists; the statutory threshold is £8,000 per 12-month period, s.95A(2)(a), cap 1%/0.5% — the 10% allowance is a mortgage-product convention). Both are recorded as corrects_site_citation; the SERVED COPY IS NOT TOUCHED (bugs_open/320 §15 — rewriting published prose on an automated finding is authority the owner withheld; his call, tracked in the lane). It also caught the AUTHOR once, recorded in the migration header: the 12-working-day period was first traced to SI 1983/1569, whose schedule covers ss.77-79/103/107-110 and NOT s.97 — the right instrument is SI 1983/1564, whose reg 4 names s.97(1) explicitly. Registering the first guess would have been this register's own defect class.

plan.summary: One data migration (699) creating loancalculator.co.uk's evidence_base site_specs row: 12 facts — 7 CCA 1974 sections (ss.56, 66A, 87, 95A, 97, 99, 100), 2 statutory instruments (SI 1983/1564 reg 4; SI 2004/1483 regs 5-6), 3 FCA Handbook rules (CONC 5.2A.5, CONC 7.3.4, DISP 1.3.1) — each with a verbatim quote verified through the production matcher with a negative control, each URL title-confirmed. Two facts carry corrects_site_citation for live copy errors found by reading the rules. Guard aborts if a register already exists; verify is DO/RAISE (a SELECT block cannot stop a COMMIT). Rollback sidecar provided. Structure copied from migration 695 (lendzy), the owner's worked example.

Facts chosen from what the SITE ACTUALLY ASSERTS (artefact crawl, 2026-09-02), prioritising the rights it leads with: the settlement-figure duty (its settlement calculator's whole premise), voluntary termination, the 14-day withdrawal, default notices, dealer-as-agent, the early-repayment compensation rules, plus the three FCA rules its guides invoke (affordability, forbearance, complaints). CONC 5.2A.5 and CONC 7.3.4 reuse lendzy's verified fact shape — same rule, same quote — RE-verified through the tool in this lane's own runs rather than trusted from their report. The moment the row exists the daily refresher starts re-fetching all 12 URLs and re-checking the quotes; HasScannableRegister arms the numeric scan, which RFC_060 §1c measured against this exact site's 474-component export with ZERO findings (the 5 false positives were on other sites, and the regulatory-citation exclusions fad209b92 are live fleet-wide).

grounded_in: RFC_060 §1b [MEASURED 2026-09-02]: 'no evidence_base at all → numeric scan never arms: 5 — lendzy.co.uk, loanzy.uk, loancash.co.uk, loancalculator.co.uk, farmerinsurance.uk'; §4: 'If only one thing happens as a result of this RFC, it should be that.'

cmd/fcaquotecheck runs, 2026-09-02, this session: 12/12 quotes true with 'zzz deliberately absent control string' false in the same run — e.g. CCA-95A: 'HTTP 200 raw=45331 visible=10099 true where more than one such payment is made in any 12 month period, the total of those payments exceeds £8,000... false zzz...'

SI 1983/1564 reg 4, verbatim from the fetched page: 'The period of 12 working days is hereby prescribed for the purposes of section 97(1) of the Act' — against the served page's 'usually within ten working days' (tools/settlement-calculator.html, crawled 2026-09-02).

CCA s.95A(2)(a)/(4), verbatim: 'the total of those payments exceeds £8,000' / 'relevant percentage means 1% ... or 0.5%' — against the served page's 'overpay up to 10% of your outstanding balance in any 12-month period without a charge' attributed to the CCA (tools/overpayment-calculator.html).

The near-miss recorded in the migration header: SI 1983/1569's schedule (fetched, read) lists ss.77(1)/78(1)/79(1)/103(1)/107-110 — NOT 97(1); the prescribed period for s.97 lives in SI 1983/1564. First-guess attribution would have committed the register's own defect class.
Migration 695 (lendzy), the owner's worked example: same guard, same DO/RAISE verify shape, same corrects_site_citation convention, same copy-not-touched rule (bugs_open/320 §15).
plan.risks: 1) This row is live the moment it applies (DB config; no image tag to roll back) — the rollback sidecar exists and its guard refuses once anything else has amended the register. 2) Arming ScanUnregisteredNumbers changes what future saves scan on this site: measured-safe per RFC_060 §1c (zero findings on this site's own component export; fad209b92's regulatory exclusions live), and the pending 397 GTM 44-page rerender wave therefore passes the armed scan with the same zero expectation — if a claims-floor refusal DOES appear on this site after apply, read it against §1c before treating it as content damage. 3) The `rule` field is human-verified until RFC_060 §3d/Q6's rule-span checker ships (approved to build 2026-09-02): neither host has rule-level URLs, so the daily check keeps quotes honest, not attributions — checked by hand against each provision's heading, dated in every fact. 4) `pinned` does not protect this row through a re-adoption (write_site_spec drops pinned — LANDMINES); the lane's standing check after any adoption run covers the identity flags and now this aspect too. 5) legislation.gov.uk serves revised text ('up to date ... 02 September 2026' banners) — a future amendment to a cited section will surface as citation drift in the daily check, which is the design, not a defect. 6) Two facts reuse lendzy's rule/quote shapes: deliberate convergence on identical external rules, re-verified independently here, not copied on trust.
